alternative_architecture.description: Use a thin feature-delivery kernel. State: separate stable product requirements from engineering policy and generated repository inventory; bind feature contracts only to relevant requirement IDs. Planning: select and clarify one near-term vertical slice, with scoped impact analysis for later canon changes instead of global reconciliation. Execution: one write-capable agent in an isolated branch/worktree, using externally enforced file and command permissions. Validation: Git/scope checks, clean Unity Edit/Play Mode tests, one fresh semantic diff review, then targeted human experiential review. Recovery: preserve the branch and attempt journal, feed specific failure evidence into at most two repairs, then escalate. Unity integration: explicitly distinguish in-memory builders from committed scenes/prefabs and require non-mutating validation. Add deterministic scheduling only after several successful deliveries.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It preserves the strongest current safety boundaries while removing global verifier swarms, duplicated state, prompt anchoring, and provider infrastructure from the gameplay critical path.

structured_output.architecture_summary: The architecture contains sound safety primitives but is not sound enough, as currently organized and implemented, for autonomous Unity delivery. It is assurance-heavy and delivery-light: canon retrieval, graph validation, evidence modeling, reconciliation, and provider transport exist, but no production path can write a gameplay change, invoke Unity, perform GER, derive readiness, dispatch, or merge. Its moving-canon model is especially weak because product design, engineering policy, and dated repository facts are mixed together and synchronized through duplicated artifacts.
structured_output.biggest_uncertainty: Actual model spend is not normalized or retained comparably. Cost severity is inferred from prompt sizes, worker counts, turn limits, retries, and history rather than invoices. Feature throughput has also never been measured through a complete production delivery.
do_not_build_yet: Progressive Decomposer and Artifact Authority platform
More provider migrations or cross-provider comparison infrastructure

evidence.observation: At the frozen clean HEAD, taskcontrol validates 37 contracts, but readiness is explicitly unavailable and zero tasks are authorized for dispatch.

The authoritative scene moved to Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity in commit 484e66a, but 16 task contracts, RESOURCE_GROUPS, PROJECT_REQUIREMENTS, and GDD canon still reference the deleted nested scene. Structural task validation nevertheless passes.
Current conformance hashes the entire GDD and marks evidence stale when that hash changes, regardless of whether the edit affects the task.
The production reconciliation prompt suite totals 4,251 lines and contains dated closure sections prescribing conclusions repaired during earlier rounds.

Nine reconciliation workers receive prior routing hints and the same complete key registry. Verifier diversity defaults to Claude opus and sonnet aliases, preserving provider-family and prompt correlation.
Parallel verification defines nine domain coverage audits plus six evidence/structure/execution audits before refiners and selective re-verification.
Production pipeline Python totals approximately 24,623 lines, compared with approximately 1,508 lines of Unity C# game code.
History contains 56 commits touching Reconciliation, 41 touching TaskGraph, and 21 touching AgentRuntime/TaskExecution/ArchitectureReview, versus 7 commits touching Assets.
Assignment 6 records two static evaluator passes followed by two human Unity runtime failures, then a refiner claim that made no Assets changes.
CURRENT_STATE first says the Codex ArchitectureReview migration is implemented, then later says Claude migration is next and Codex remains unimplemented.

Read-only checks executed successfully: taskcontrol validate, taskcontrol ready, NSC-023 state, and GDDRAG validate. HEAD/tree and the worktree remained unchanged; NSC-023 is the sole demonstrated conformant production task.

gdd_iteration_concerns: The root GDD mixes gameplay intent, agent workflow policy, package choices, build configuration, and dated repository inventory. An engineering change can therefore appear to be a game-design change.
Whole-document hashing creates global revalidation pressure from unrelated canon edits.
Sequential RAG chunk IDs are reproducible but are not durable requirement identities across heading insertion or reordering.
Task contracts copy GDD prose and bootstrap repository observations, creating stale replicas instead of durable references.
No demonstrated workflow maps a changed clause to only the affected contracts, code/assets, tests, and evidence.
The scene relocation proves synchronization is not transactional: production code, tests, and evidence moved while canon, resource claims, and task evidence did not.
Routine GDD evolution needs a reviewed requirement-level impact workflow. Full reconciliation should be an exceptional audit, not the normal synchronization mechanism.
human_intervention_points: Approve ambiguous gameplay mechanics and input arbitration. NSC-003 currently lacks enough decisions for a safe handoff.
Approve genuine canon or architecture changes rather than letting an agent infer design.
Perform Play Mode, input-feel, framing, readability, animation, visual-quality, and balance judgments.
Inspect scene, prefab, package, and build-setting changes where serialization or editor behavior matters.
Review and merge initially; merge automation should wait for repeated delivery evidence.
Decide whether a circuit-breaker failure requires repair, task rescoping, contract change, or design change.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: AgentRuntime exact-type, polymorphic-container, Windows device-name, deep-JSON, and immutable-publication hardening protects mostly adversarial transport cases not experienced during game delivery.
Evidence-record cycle, incomparable-ancestry, and ambiguity logic is covered synthetically but has no real production revalidation history.
GitHub mirroring, leases, merge queues, and parallel resource scheduling address future scale, not the current single-worker bottleneck.
Artifact Authority and style GER address future generated design/content; the current graph has zero artifact tasks.
Eight-role ArchitectureReview provider provenance and future cross-provider comparison do not advance gameplay delivery.
Automatic backlog replenishment and continuous supervision protect a future autonomous queue that does not yet exist.
missing_components: A production end-to-end gameplay lane from approved contract through implementation, Unity validation, review, merge, and evidence.
Stable requirement/clause identities and scoped GDD-change impact links.
A write-capable worker boundary and externally enforced approved command execution.
Production ExecutionCrew/GER integration, or a substantially thinner equivalent.
Restartable attempt/lease state for one real task.
Cross-representation referential validation covering canon-described paths, task resource claims, builders, tests, and actual Unity assets.
Per-feature token, latency, retry, defect, and human-minute telemetry.
A real production revalidation example; only NSC-023 has a baseline.

deliverables: Obtain a one-page human-approved input decision covering click/hold semantics, UI/gameplay arbitration, destination replacement and cancellation, arrival tolerance, and pathing expectations.

Supersede or split NSC-003. Make the first contract cover shared pointer projection plus visible click-to-destination/hold-steer movement; defer restriction/reset/suspend APIs unless required by the implementation seam.
Correct the authoritative scene path across GDD engineering facts, task/resource claims, and project requirements, then add one deterministic cross-representation path check.
Implement the movement slice in one isolated branch using Input Actions, shared gameplay-plane projection, scene-builder wiring, and the committed Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity artifact.
Run clean targeted Edit/Play Mode validation, obtain human movement-feel approval, perform one fresh semantic diff review, merge, and publish one compact delivery receipt.
next_slice.proof_of_value: Within one working day, an approved brief becomes merged, visibly playable mouse-directed movement with clean Unity evidence, bounded model usage, no global reconciliation, and no manual repair of duplicated operational state. Record elapsed time, model calls/tokens where available, repair count, escaped defects, and human minutes.

next_slice.why: It is player-visible, unlocks Fireball, Frost Field, and door targeting, and tests the actual value proposition more directly than another infrastructure milestone.

observed_failure_solutions: Runtime evidence re-entering GER directly addresses the camera’s two static-pass/runtime-fail incidents.

No-op detection and circuit breakers address the observed refiner claim that made no Assets change. Progress should, however, be tied to resolving a named failure rather than merely producing any diff.
The non-saving in-memory scene-builder seam and clean Unity runner address observed canonical-scene mutation risk from builder tests.
Production GDDRAG freshness and integrity replace the actually stale July Assignment 4 knowledge base.
Scene centralization and meta-identity checks address the earlier duplicate authoritative-scene ambiguity.
Raw-output preservation, bounded retries, finding identities, and deterministic validators address observed reconciliation parsing, max-turn, dangling-edge, attribution, and refinement failures.
Separating task contracts from mutable completion status closes a discovered authority vulnerability, although no bad autonomous dispatch actually occurred.
overengineering: Approximately 24.6k lines of pipeline Python precede a single write-capable gameplay execution lane.
A 37-task graph was produced through nine generation workers and up to fifteen parallel auditors, with refiners and selective pass two layered afterward.
The 4,251-line reconciliation prompt suite accumulates specific closure patches, raising maintenance cost and anchoring future reviewers.
AgentRuntime heavily hardens hostile JSON and path cases in a trusted single-user environment while repository writing and approved command execution remain unsupported.
ArchitectureReview provider migration proves transport reuse, not game-development throughput.
WORK_ID_MAP and persisted resource-group membership duplicate relationships derivable from task contracts.
CURRENT_STATE, START_HERE, master context, milestone documents, ADR summaries, and reconciliation current views duplicate present-tense state and have already diverged.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary authorities are: human-approved product canon; bounded feature/task contracts; integrated Git state; isolated attempt state; deterministic test/runtime evidence; human experiential approval; and derived readiness/merge state.
The current separation of task definition from completion evidence is sound. Model/provider claims also correctly lack test, merge, or conformance authority.
Dated repository inventory and pipeline architecture should not live in root game-design canon. Put them in generated repository facts and engineering policy.

Reconciliation snapshots are useful audit history, but Tasks, WORK_ID_MAP, RESOURCE_GROUPS, PROJECT_REQUIREMENTS, copied GDD prose, current-state documents, and mutable reconciliation views duplicate responsibility.
Conformance is simultaneously under-sensitive and over-sensitive: manually chosen surfaces may omit causal dependencies, while a whole-GDD hash invalidates unrelated tasks.
Resource-group files duplicate task claims and validate internal agreement rather than whether the referenced Unity resource still exists.
GitHub may become a dashboard, but it must not become a second operational authority without a single explicit owner.

The GDD assigns humans architecture, merging, scene inspection, playtesting, balance, and final integration. The resulting system is assisted development, not high autonomy, until some of those steps are safely narrowed or automated.
strong_decisions: Deterministic tools own graph computation, Git identity, schema checks, test execution facts, and clean-tree checks.
Workers and providers cannot self-declare delivery, conformance, readiness, or authorization.
Runtime and Unity evidence can override a semantic/static pass.
Task definitions are separated from current completion truth.
Branches/worktrees should precede parallelism, and Unity shared-asset locking should be conservative.
RAG is correctly treated as canon retrieval rather than repository truth.
Progressive decomposition and explicit human authority for missing design are sensible principles.
Starting with one worker and bounding retries is appropriate.
The testing policy correctly distinguishes builder capability from committed-artifact conformance.
structural_flaws: Evolving design is framed mainly as snapshot reconciliation and invalidation instead of routine scoped change management.
Verification independence is overstated because workers share canon, candidate framing, prior routing keys, the key registry, provider family, and prescriptive closure prompts.
Unioning every verifier finding reduces false-negative risk but amplifies false-positive cost and destabilizes reconciliation.
The production critical path is missing: no write-capable task execution, orchestrated Unity run, production GER, readiness, dispatch, or merge.
Deterministic checks are strongest at artifact shape and transport boundaries but miss cross-representation referential integrity, as the deleted scene path demonstrates.
The no-op rule can incentivize irrelevant churn. Assignment 6’s final pass added null-target hardening while the substantive framing repair had already occurred elsewhere.
The milestone sequence optimized architecture assurance before feature throughput and has become self-reinforcing.
Provider-neutrality is implemented below an absent product workflow; abstraction arrived before the first production consumer that matters.
structured_output.throughput_assessment: Current near-term leverage is low. The system can retrieve canon, validate graph shape, inspect one camera baseline, and harden model transport, but it cannot autonomously advance gameplay. Dispatch is disabled, workers cannot write or run approved commands, Unity/GER is not integrated, and only one task has production evidence. The machinery may improve assurance after attachment to a delivery lane, but it is not currently credible for turning weeks into days. A thin single-feature lane could plausibly create major leverage quickly; the planned supervisor, decomposer, GitHub, and parallel-worker milestones would not.
structured_output.verdict_reason: The core philosophy is sound, but the current architecture is partially unsound because its moving-canon and state-synchronization model has already drifted, semantic verification is correlated and prompt-anchored, and most investment lies outside the gameplay-delivery critical path. Preserve deterministic evidence, runtime validation, isolation, bounded retries, and human design authority. Reorganize around one real feature at a time and freeze or remove infrastructure that does not measurably reduce delivery time or escaped defects.
